source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. X (Montreuil)

2.title: Explanatio litteralis capituli secundi: Et nunc ad vos mandatum hoc, o sacerdotes.
2.title_en: Literal explanation of the second chapter: And now, O ye priests, this commandment is to you.

paras.t: Consequenter Dominus hortatur sacerdotes ad pœnitentiam, adjiciendo minas, ut qui se amore boni et zelo æquitatis non corrigunt, timore supplicii corrigantur. Et nunc ad vos mandatum hoc de observatione cultus divini in cæremoniis templi, o sacerdotes, dirigitur. Sacerdotibus quippe correctis, ceteri facilius emendantur. Si nolueritis audire auribus mentis et corporis, et si nolueritis ponere super cor, id est diligenter advertere, recolere et implere quod jubeo, ut detis gloriam nomini meo, id est, debitam mihi reverentiam impendatis, et coram aliis me clarificetis, gloriosum annuntietis, et omne mihi bonum adscribatis, ait Dominus exercituum; mittam in vos egestatem, id est terræ sterilitatem, victualiumque inopiam: quam carnales cupidique Judæi plurimum abhorrebant, præsertim quum in Deuteronomio Moyses scripserit, Omnino indigens et mendicus non erit inter vos; et maledicam benedictionibus vestris, id est fructibus terræ et ceteris bonis terrenis, quæ mea benedictione habetis, quibus et vos benedicere consuevistis, et maledicam illis, auferendo a vobis hæc dona, et opposita mala super vos inducendo; quoniam non posuistis super cor, id est, præcepta mea non impressistis memoriæ, nec debite custodistis. Quocontra dicit Psalmographus: In corde meo abscondi eloquia tua, ut non peccem tibi. Et Salomon ait: Serva mandata et legem quasi pupillam oculi tui. Liga eam in digitis tuis, et in tabulis cordis tui scribe eam.
paras.en: Next the Lord exhorts the priests to penance, adding threats, so that those who do not amend themselves out of love of the good and zeal for equity may be amended by fear of punishment. [[2:1|And now|Et nunc]] [[2:1|this commandment|mandatum hoc]], concerning the observance of divine worship in the ceremonies of the temple, is directed [[2:1|to you|ad vos]], [[2:1|O ye priests|o sacerdotes]]. For once the priests are corrected, the rest are more easily amended. [[2:2|If you will not hear|Si nolueritis audire]] with the ears of mind and body, [[2:2|and if you will not lay it to heart|et si nolueritis ponere super cor]], that is, diligently attend to, call to mind and fulfil what I command, [[2:2|to give glory to my name|ut detis gloriam nomini meo]], that is, pay me the reverence due to me, glorify me before others, proclaim me glorious, and ascribe every good to me, [[2:2|saith the Lord of hosts|ait Dominus exercituum]]: [[2:2|I will send poverty upon you|mittam in vos egestatem]], that is, barrenness of the land and want of victuals: which the carnal and covetous Jews greatly abhorred, especially since Moses had written in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 15:4|there shall be no poor nor beggar among you|Omnino indigens et mendicus non erit inter vos]]; [[2:2|and will curse your blessings|et maledicam benedictionibus vestris]], that is, the fruits of the earth and the other earthly goods which you have by my blessing, and with which you too were wont to bless, [[2:2|yea I will curse them|et maledicam illis]], by taking these gifts away from you and bringing the opposite evils upon you; [[2:2|because you have not laid it to heart|quoniam non posuistis super cor]], that is, you have not impressed my precepts on your memory, nor kept them as you ought. Against this the Psalmist says: [[Ps 118:11|Thy words have I hidden in my heart, that I may not sin against thee|In corde meo abscondi eloquia tua, ut non peccem tibi]]. And Solomon says: [[Prov 7:2|Keep my commandments|Serva mandata]] [[Prov 7:2|and my law as the apple of thy eye|et legem quasi pupillam oculi tui]]. [[Prov 7:3|Bind it upon thy fingers, write it upon the tables of thy heart|Liga eam in digitis tuis, et in tabulis cordis tui scribe eam]].

paras.t: Ecce ego projiciam vobis brachium, id est armum animalis dextrum mihi oblatum, quia propter vestra peccata munus vestrum non habeo gratum, et dispergam super vultum vestrum stercus solennitatum vestrarum, id est, immunditiam vitiorum quæ in festis vestris committitis, et irreverentiam quam mihi facitis, in vos manifeste convertam, vos confundendo ac puniendo. Vel per stercus istud, intelligitur caro oblata continens stercora, quam Deus ob eorum peccata non acceptavit, sed eis rejecit. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt: Dispergam ventriculum, etc. Et assumet vos secum, id est, contemptibiles fœdique vitiis eritis, sicut stercus: ut tales sint offerentes, qualia ea quæ offerunt.
paras.en: [[2:3|Behold, I will cast the shoulder to you|Ecce ego projiciam vobis brachium]], that is, the right shoulder of the animal offered to me, because on account of your sins I do not hold your gift acceptable; [[2:3|and will scatter upon your face the dung of your solemnities|et dispergam super vultum vestrum stercus solennitatum vestrarum]], that is, the uncleanness of the vices which you commit on your feasts, and the irreverence which you show me, I will openly turn back upon you, confounding and punishing you. Or by this dung is understood the flesh offered with the dung still in it, which God did not accept because of their sins, but threw back at them. Hence the Septuagint translated: I will scatter the paunch, etc. [[2:3|and it shall take you away with it|Et assumet vos secum]], that is, you will be contemptible and foul with vices, like dung: so that the offerers are such as the things they offer.

paras.t: Et scietis, per justitiæ meæ effectum experientiamque vindictæ, quia misi ad vos mandatum istud, jam dictum, ut esset pactum meum, id est testamentum vel fœdus de modo sacrificiorum, cum Levi, id est Levitis ad cultum Dei specialiter dedicatis: quos etiam Deus jussit præ aliis, maculis mentis corporisque carere, et virtutum ornatu fulgere, juxta illud Exodi, Sacerdotes qui accedunt ad Dominum, sanctificentur, ne percutiat eos; dicit Dominus exercituum.
paras.en: [[2:4|And you shall know|Et scietis]], by the effect of my justice and the experience of my vengeance, [[2:4|that I sent you this commandment|quia misi ad vos mandatum istud]] already spoken of, [[2:4|that my covenant might be|ut esset pactum meum]], that is, the testament or compact concerning the manner of the sacrifices, [[2:4|with Levi|cum Levi]], that is, with the Levites, specially dedicated to the worship of God: whom God also commanded, above others, to be free of the stains of mind and body and to shine with the adornment of the virtues, according to that of Exodus: [[Ex 19:22|The priests also that come to the Lord, let them be sanctified, lest he strike them|Sacerdotes qui accedunt ad Dominum, sanctificentur, ne percutiat eos]]; [[2:4|saith the Lord of hosts|dicit Dominus exercituum]].

paras.t: Pactum meum fuit cum eo vitæ et pacis, id est, pactum vitæ et pacis percussi et inii cum tribu Levitica in deserto, eligens illam ad sacerdotium, et promittens eidem, quod si ipsa ac populus legem meam servarent, in pace viverent super terram, imo pacem pectoris et vitam gratiæ obtinerent. Porro, ut hic ait Hieronymus, quidquid nunc de Levi asseritur, ad sacerdotes et potissime ad pontifices legis Moysis pertinet. Et dedi ei timorem meum, non servilem dumtaxat, sed filialem et castum, et timuit me, et a facie nominis mei, id est consideratione majestatis meæ, pavebat. Istud in Moyse, Aaron, Eleazaro, Phinees, multisque aliis de tribu Levi exortis fuit impletum, imo et in patriarcha Levi, qui etsi interdum peccavit, postea tamen virtuosæ fuisse creditur vitæ.
paras.en: [[2:5|My covenant was with him of life and peace|Pactum meum fuit cum eo vitæ et pacis]], that is, I struck and entered into a covenant of life and peace with the tribe of Levi in the desert, choosing it for the priesthood and promising it that, if it and the people kept my law, they would live in peace upon the land, nay more, would obtain peace of heart and the life of grace. Moreover, as Jerome says here, whatever is now asserted of Levi belongs to the priests, and above all to the high priests, of the law of Moses. [[2:5|and I gave him fear|Et dedi ei timorem]] of me, not servile fear only, but filial and chaste fear [chaste fear: the fear of a loving son, who dreads to offend, as against servile fear, which dreads punishment], [[2:5|and he feared me|et timuit me]], and [[2:5|before my name|et a facie nominis mei]], that is, at the thought of my majesty, [[2:5|he was afraid|pavebat]]. This was fulfilled in Moses, Aaron, Eleazar, Phinees, and many others sprung from the tribe of Levi, nay, in the patriarch Levi too, who, though he sinned at times, is nevertheless believed to have led a virtuous life afterwards.

paras.t: Lex veritatis, scilicet lex divinitus data per Moysen, fuit in ore ejus, id est filiorum Levi, de quibus nunc dictum est, qui populum instruxerunt; et iniquitas non est inventa in labiis ejus: non quod isti ab omni iniquitate immunes exstiterint, sed quia condigne pœnituerint, et gratiam sanctitatis sortiti sint: sicut de se ipso fatetur Apostolus, Nihil mihi conscius sum; qui tamen alias loquitur, Venit Jesus peccatores salvos facere, quorum ego primus sum. In pace, id est mentis tranquillitate, et in æquitate, id est justa conversatione, ambulavit mecum, id est coram me et secundum beneplacitum meum mihi conjunctus per voluntatis conformitatem, et multos avertit ab iniquitate. Moyses enim et Aaron ac reliqui quidam posteri Aaron, plures de genere Israel ad pœnitentiam induxerunt, atque a vitiis variis retraxerunt.
paras.en: [[2:6|The law of truth|Lex veritatis]], namely the law given by God through Moses, [[2:6|was in his mouth|fuit in ore ejus]], that is, in the mouth of the sons of Levi of whom we have just spoken, who instructed the people; [[2:6|and iniquity was not found in his lips|et iniquitas non est inventa in labiis ejus]]: not that these men were free from all iniquity, but because they did fitting penance and obtained the grace of holiness: as the Apostle confesses of himself: [[1 Cor 4:4|I am not conscious to myself of anything|Nihil mihi conscius sum]]; who yet says elsewhere: [[1 Tim 1:15|Christ Jesus came|Venit Jesus]] [[1 Tim 1:15|to save sinners, of whom I am the chief|peccatores salvos facere, quorum ego primus sum]]. [[2:6|in peace|In pace]], that is, in tranquillity of mind, [[2:6|and in equity|et in æquitate]], that is, in an upright manner of life, [[2:6|he walked with me|ambulavit mecum]], that is, before me and according to my good pleasure, joined to me by conformity of will, [[2:6|and turned many away from iniquity|et multos avertit ab iniquitate]]. For Moses and Aaron, and some others of Aaron's descendants, led many of the race of Israel to penance and drew them back from various vices.

paras.t: Labia enim sacerdotis custodiunt scientiam: id est, ad sacerdotum officium pertinet congruo tempore doctrinam legis divinæ plebi proponere, et scientiam salutarem in aliis conservare. Ideo in pectore summi sacerdotis fuerat rationale, in quo Doctrina et Veritas ponebatur, quia sacerdos doctus esse debet, et præco veritatis divinæ. Et legem requirent subditi et vulgares, ex ore ejus. Unde dicit Apostolus ad Titum: Oportet episcopum sine crimine esse, amplectentem eum qui secundum doctrinam est, fidelem sermonem, ut potens sit exhortari in doctrina sana, et eos qui contradicunt, arguere; quia angelus, id est nuntius, Domini exercituum est. Quemadmodum enim divinus Dionysius docet, infimum ordinis superioris, et supremum ordinis inferioris, magnam habent mutuo convenientiam, et nomen unius transfertur ad aliud. Quum ergo in cœlesti hierarchia ordo angelorum sit infimus, et in ecclesiastica hierarchia ordo sacerdotum sit summus, angeli et sacerdotes in multis communicant: ita ut sacerdotes angeli nuncupentur, quoniam inter Deum et populum mediando, et ea quæ Dei sunt, hominibus nuntiando, atque spiritualem et angelicam vitam in carne ducendo, angelicum exercent officium. Ideo in Apocalypsi episcopi septem Ecclesiarum in Asia, angeli appellantur.
paras.en: [[2:7|For the lips of the priests shall keep knowledge|Labia enim sacerdotis custodiunt scientiam]]: that is, it belongs to the office of priests to set the teaching of the divine law before the people at the fitting time, and to preserve saving knowledge in others. Therefore on the breast of the high priest was the rational, in which Doctrine and Truth were placed[[Ex 28:29||]][[Ex 28:30||]] [the rational: the breastplate of judgment worn by the high priest], because the priest ought to be learned and a herald of the divine truth. [[2:7|and they shall seek the law|Et legem requirent]], namely subjects and common folk, [[2:7|at his mouth|ex ore ejus]]. Hence the Apostle says to Titus: [[Tit 1:7|a bishop must be without crime|Oportet episcopum sine crimine esse]], [[Tit 1:9|Embracing that faithful word which is according to doctrine, that he may be able to exhort in sound doctrine and to convince the gainsayers|amplectentem eum qui secundum doctrinam est, fidelem sermonem, ut potens sit exhortari in doctrina sana, et eos qui contradicunt, arguere]]; [[2:7|because he is the angel|quia angelus]], that is, the messenger, [[2:7|of the Lord of hosts|Domini exercituum est]]. For as the divine Dionysius teaches, the lowest of a higher order and the highest of a lower order have a great likeness to each other, and the name of the one is carried over to the other. Since, then, in the heavenly hierarchy the order of angels is the lowest, and in the ecclesiastical hierarchy the order of priests is the highest, angels and priests have much in common: so that priests are called angels, since by mediating between God and the people, announcing to men the things of God, and leading a spiritual and angelic life in the flesh, they exercise the office of angels. Therefore in the Apocalypse the bishops of the seven Churches in Asia are called angels[[Apoc 1:20||]][[Apoc 2:1||]][[Apoc 2:8||]].

paras.t: Vos autem recessistis de via, id est, legem Dei qua itur ad vitam beatam, non custodistis, et scandalizastis, id est, dicto vel facto vestro inordinato plurimos ad ruinam peccati traxistis, in lege scripta, quam non servastis. Irritum fecistis pactum Levi, dicit Dominus exercituum, id est, pactum cum Levi seu tribu sacerdotali initum de sacrificiis templi, sprevistis.
paras.en: [[2:8|But you have departed out of the way|Vos autem recessistis de via]], that is, you have not kept the law of God by which one goes to the life of bliss, [[2:8|and have caused many to stumble|et scandalizastis]], that is, by your disordered word or deed you have drawn [[2:8|many|plurimos]] to the ruin of sin, [[2:8|at the law|in lege]], the written law, which you have not observed. [[2:8|you have made void the covenant of Levi, saith the Lord of hosts|Irritum fecistis pactum Levi, dicit Dominus exercituum]], that is, you have spurned the covenant made with Levi, or the priestly tribe, concerning the sacrifices of the temple.

paras.t: Propter quod et ego dedi vos contemptibiles et humiles, id est abjectos, omnibus populis, inter quos captivi fuistis, vel qui vestram calamitatem noverunt. Unde in libro Esdræ scriptum est: Audi, Deus noster, quia facti sumus despectui. Sicut non servastis vias meas, id est divina præcepta. Hinc primo Regum Dominus protestatur: Quicumque glorificaverit me, glorificabo eum; qui autem contemnunt me, erunt ignobiles. Et accepistis faciem in lege, id est, personas, non causas, adspexistis, judicando injuste propter munera, vel timore aut favore, potentes, divites et nobiles inferioribus præponendo. Quo contra in Psalmo habetur: Usquequo judicatis iniquitatem (id est, judicando approbatis peccatores), et facies peccatorum sumitis?
paras.en: [[2:9|Therefore have I also made you contemptible, and base|Propter quod et ego dedi vos contemptibiles et humiles]], that is, abject, [[2:9|before all people|omnibus populis]] among whom you have been captives, or who have known your calamity. Hence it is written in the book of Esdras: [[2 Esd 4:4|Hear thou our God, for we are despised|Audi, Deus noster, quia facti sumus despectui]]. [[2:9|as you have not kept my ways|Sicut non servastis vias meas]], that is, the divine precepts. Hence the Lord protests in the first book of Kings: [[1 Kings 2:30|whosoever shall glorify me, him will I glorify: but they that despise me, shall be despised|Quicumque glorificaverit me, glorificabo eum; qui autem contemnunt me, erunt ignobiles]]. [[2:9|and have accepted persons in the law|Et accepistis faciem in lege]], that is, you have looked to persons, not to causes, judging unjustly for bribes, or out of fear or favour, preferring the powerful, the rich and the noble to those beneath them. Against this it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 81:2|How long will you judge unjustly|Usquequo judicatis iniquitatem]] [literally 'judge iniquity'] (that is, by your judging approve sinners), [[Ps 81:2|and accept the persons of the wicked|et facies peccatorum sumitis]]?

paras.t: Consequenter increpat Judæorum superbiam. Numquid non pater unus omnium nostrum est? scilicet Adam, vel etiam Abraham. Numquid non Deus unus creavit nos? qui ait in Deuteronomio: Videte quod ego sim solus, et non sit alius Deus præter me. Animas nempe singulorum condidit Deus sigillatim et per se ipsum immediate; corpora quoque nostra ab ipso originaliter sunt creata. Quare ergo despicit unusquisque nostrum fratrem, id est proximum suum, violans pactum patrum nostrorum, id est in hoc ipso transgrediens præceptum patribus datum de proximo diligendo ac sustentando? Hinc Isaias minatur: Væ qui spernis, nonne et ipse sperneris?
paras.en: Next he rebukes the pride of the Jews. [[2:10|Have we not all one father|Numquid non pater unus omnium nostrum]]? namely Adam, or even Abraham. [[2:10|hath not one God created us|Numquid non Deus unus creavit nos]]? who says in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 32:39|See ye that I alone am, and there is no other God besides me|Videte quod ego sim solus, et non sit alius Deus præter me]]. For God created the souls of each one singly[[Ps 32:15||]], by himself and immediately; our bodies too were created by him in their origin. [[2:10|why then doth every one of us despise his brother|Quare ergo despicit unusquisque nostrum fratrem]], that is, his neighbour, [[2:10|violating the covenant of our fathers|violans pactum patrum nostrorum]], that is, by this very thing transgressing the precept given to the fathers about loving and supporting one's neighbour[[Ex 20:13||]] [the margin gives Exod. xx, 13–17]? Hence Isaias threatens: [[Is 33:1|Woe to thee|Væ]], [[Is 33:1|thou that despisest, shalt not thyself also be despised|qui spernis, nonne et ipse sperneris]]?

paras.t: Transgressus est Juda, id est, populus Juda de Babylone reversus, legem Dei non custodivit; et abominatio, id est irrationabilis prorsus transgressio, facta est in Israel et in Jerusalem, id est a filiis Israel incolisque Jerusalem post reditum de Chaldæa: quia in templi ædificatione, sacrificiorum oblatione, sabbati observatione, et alienigenarum uxorum acceptione, negligentes fuerunt, ut patet in libro Esdræ, et alibi. Quia contaminavit Judas sanctificationem Domini, quam dilexit, id est, templum Dei inhonoravit: de quo dicitur primo libro Machabæorum, quod Antiochus intravit sanctificationem cum superbia. Vel sanctificatio ista, est cultus Dei in sacrificiis et ceteris latriæ actibus Deo placentibus; et habuit filiam dei alieni. Judæi enim uxores gentiles idolorum servitrices acceperunt, ut dictum est sæpe.
paras.en: [[2:11|Juda hath transgressed|Transgressus est Juda]], that is, the people of Juda, returned from Babylon, did not keep the law of God; [[2:11|and abomination|et abominatio]], that is, an utterly unreasonable transgression, [[2:11|hath been committed in Israel, and in Jerusalem|facta est in Israel et in Jerusalem]], that is, by the children of Israel and the dwellers in Jerusalem after the return from Chaldea: for they were negligent in building the temple, in offering the sacrifices, in keeping the sabbath, and in taking foreign wives, as is plain in the book of Esdras[[1 Esd 9:1||]], and elsewhere[[2 Esd 13:1||]]. [[2:11|for Juda hath profaned the holiness of the Lord, which he loved|Quia contaminavit Judas sanctificationem Domini, quam dilexit]], that is, he dishonoured the temple of God: of which it is said in the first book of Machabees that Antiochus [[1 Mach 1:23|proudly entered into the sanctuary|intravit sanctificationem cum superbia]] [the Latin word is *sanctificatio*, the same as 'holiness' in this verse]. Or this holiness is the worship of God in the sacrifices and the other acts of latria [that is, the worship due to God alone] that are pleasing to God; [[2:11|and hath married the daughter of a strange god|et habuit filiam dei alieni]]. For the Jews took gentile wives, servants of idols, as has often been said.

paras.t: Disperdat Dominus virum qui fecerit hoc amplius in futuro. Quasi dicat: Quod factum est, Deus indulgeat. Vel dicitur hoc zelo justitiæ, nisi pœniteant; vel modo propheticæ prænuntiationis, quod utique dispergentur, nisi se inde correxerint. Magistrum et discipulum, id est doctum et simplicem instructorem peccati, et qui ei consentit, magnum et parvum, qui est de tabernaculo Jacob, id est de ejus familia. Vel sensus est, quod tales transgressores ab aliis bonis Judæis disperderentur modo jam tacto. Et offerentem munus Domino exercituum, id est, etiam sacerdotem Deo sacrificantem ita peccantem, Deus disperdat, si in peccato permanserit.
paras.en: [[2:12|The Lord will cut off the man that hath done this|Disperdat Dominus virum qui fecerit hoc]] [Denis reads *Disperdat*, 'may the Lord cut off', where the Vulgate has *Disperdet*, 'will cut off'] from now on in the future. As if he said: What has been done, may God pardon. Or this is said out of zeal for justice, unless they repent; or by way of prophetic foretelling, that they will surely be scattered unless they amend themselves in this. [[2:12|both the master, and the scholar|Magistrum et discipulum]], that is, the learned and the simple, the one who teaches sin and the one who consents to him, great and small, who is [[2:12|out of the tabernacles of Jacob|de tabernaculo Jacob]], that is, of his household. Or the sense is that such transgressors would be cut off by the other, good Jews, in the way already touched upon. [[2:12|and him that offereth an offering to the Lord of hosts|Et offerentem munus Domino exercituum]], that is, may God cut off even the priest who sacrifices to God while sinning in this way, if he remains in his sin.

paras.t: Et hoc malum quod subditur rursum fecistis, adjiciendo peccata peccatis. Operiebatis lacrimis altare Domini, fletu et gemitu: id est, uxores vestras priores Judæas vobiscum de Babylone redeuntes, per hoc quod eas propter earum deformitatem vel senectutem abjecistis, et alienigenas accepistis, induxistis et compulistis ad hoc, quod coram altari quotidie flebant cum gemitu coram me, contra vos conquerentes quod taliter abjicerentur. Ita exponit Hieronymus. Alii autem exponunt, quod ipsi viri sic lacrimabantur, putantes peccatum hoc expiare absque rejectione uxorum gentilium: quod fuit erroneum. Ita ut ultra non respiciam ad sacrificium mihi a vobis oblatum, nec accipiam placabile quid, id est aliquam hostiam expiationis, de manu vestra, donec a præfatis vitiis vos emendetis.
paras.en: [[2:13|And this|Et hoc]] evil which is now added [[2:13|again have you done|rursum fecistis]], adding sins to sins. [[2:13|you have covered the altar of the Lord with tears, with weeping|Operiebatis lacrimis altare Domini, fletu]], and groaning [Denis reads *gemitu*, 'groaning', where the Vulgate has *mugitu*, 'bellowing']: that is, your former wives, Jewesses, who came back with you from Babylon, you have driven and compelled, by casting them off for their plainness or their age and taking foreign women, to weep daily with groaning before the altar in my presence, complaining against you that they were cast off in this way. So Jerome explains it. Others, however, explain that the men themselves wept thus, thinking to expiate this sin without putting away their gentile wives: which was an error. [[2:13|so that I have no more a regard to sacrifice|Ita ut ultra non respiciam ad sacrificium]] offered to me by you, [[2:13|neither do I accept any atonement|nec accipiam placabile quid]], that is, any victim of expiation, [[2:13|at your hands|de manu vestra]], until you amend yourselves of the aforesaid vices.

paras.t: Et dixistis: Quam ob causam? Videlicet, Quia Dominus testificatus est inter te et uxorem pubertatis tuæ: id est, Deus in Genesi dixit, quod tu et uxor tua legitima simul maneretis, ac mutuo diligeretis: Relinquet, inquiens, homo patrem suum et matrem suam, et adhærebit uxori suæ, et erunt duo in carne una; quam tu despexisti, aliam superinducendo, et ipsam quasi ancillam tenendo. Et hæc particeps tua, id est, uxor ista esse debet consors ac socia tua, non famula: ideo enim mulier de latere viri plasmata est. Adam quoque dixit ad Dominum: Mulier quam dedisti mihi sociam, dedit mihi de ligno, et comedi. Et uxor fœderis tui, id est, cum qua fœdus amicitiæ animæque consensum tenere debes.
paras.en: [[2:14|And you have said: For what cause|Et dixistis: Quam ob causam]]? Namely, [[2:14|Because the Lord hath been witness between thee, and the wife of thy youth|Quia Dominus testificatus est inter te et uxorem pubertatis tuæ]]: that is, God said in Genesis that thou and thy lawful wife should remain together and love one another: [[Gen 2:24|a man shall leave|Relinquet]], he says, [[Gen 2:24|father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they shall be two in one flesh|homo patrem suum et matrem suam, et adhærebit uxori suæ, et erunt duo in carne una]]; [[2:14|whom thou hast despised|quam tu despexisti]], by bringing in another over her and keeping her as a kind of handmaid. [[2:14|yet she was thy partner|Et hæc particeps tua]], that is, this wife ought to be thy consort and companion, not a servant: for this is why woman was formed from the side of man. Adam too said to the Lord: [[Gen 3:12|The woman, whom thou gavest me to be my companion, gave me of the tree, and I did eat|Mulier quam dedisti mihi sociam, dedit mihi de ligno, et comedi]]. [[2:14|and the wife of thy covenant|Et uxor fœderis tui]], that is, the one with whom thou oughtest to keep a compact of friendship and agreement of soul.

paras.t: Nonne unus fecit, id est, idem Creator unusque Deus plasmavit Adam et Evam, seu virum et feminam, et residuum spiritus ejus est, id est hoc quod sibi cohærent per amorem et cohabitationem, præter id quod ab uno Deo creati sunt? Hoc est spiritus Dei, id est, voluntatis divinæ. Et quid unus quærit? id est, quid Deus intendit per hoc, quod vult a filiis Israel Judæas uxores teneri, vel primam conjugem non relinqui, nec alienigenas duci? nisi semen Dei, id est filios qui divino cultui educentur. Ideo mulier si deformis est vel egena, sperni non debet nec abjici. Custodite ergo spiritum vestrum, id est animam a ruina peccati, et uxorem adolescentiæ tuæ noli despicere, quam in adolescentia accepisti: ut quæ tibi virginali primum juncta est matrimonio, perseveret usque ad vitæ finem.
paras.en: [[2:15|Did not one make her|Nonne unus fecit]], that is, did not the same Creator, the one God, form Adam and Eve, or man and woman, [[2:15|and she is the residue of his spirit|et residuum spiritus ejus est]] [*residuum*: what is left over], that is, the fact that they cleave to each other by love and by living together, over and above their having been created by the one God? This is of the spirit of God, that is, of the divine will. [[2:15|And what doth one seek|Et quid unus quærit]]? that is, what does God intend in willing that the children of Israel keep Jewish wives, or that the first wife be not forsaken, nor foreign women taken? [[2:15|but the seed of God|nisi semen Dei]], that is, children to be brought up for the worship of God. Therefore a woman, if she is plain or poor, ought not to be spurned or cast off. [[2:15|Keep then your spirit|Custodite ergo spiritum vestrum]], that is, your soul, from the ruin of sin, [[2:15|and despise not the wife of thy youth|et uxorem adolescentiæ tuæ noli despicere]], whom thou didst take in thy youth: so that she who was first joined to thee in virginal marriage may remain with thee until the end of life.

paras.t: Quum odio habueris eam, dimitte, dicit Dominus Deus Israel, dando ipsi libellum repudii. Quod autem Dominus dicat hoc permissive ad vitandum deterius, scilicet uxoricidium, sicut permisit Judæis usuram ad alienos, non absolute vel imperative, innotescit ex eo quod subditur: Operiet autem iniquitas viri conjugem repudiantis ex odio, vel causa non justa, vestimentum ejus, dicit Dominus exercituum, id est, in corpore suo debitam luet pœnam in igne inferni, nisi vere pœniteat, quatenus in quo peccavit, in illo et puniatur. Vel, Operiet iniquitas vestimentum ejus, id est, peccatum ejus ducetur in lucem, et omnibus in judicio ostendetur, sicut apparet quod in vestimenti superficie situatur. Custodite spiritum vestrum, et nolite despicere conjugem primam atque legitimam. Hinc Christus in Evangelio docet, uxorem non esse abjiciendam, nisi ob fornicationem: nec tunc relinquitur quantum ad vinculum matrimoniale, quum sit insolubile post copulam carnalem, sed quoad cohabitationem ac torum.
paras.en: [[2:16|When thou shalt hate her put her away, saith the Lord, the God of Israel|Quum odio habueris eam, dimitte, dicit Dominus Deus Israel]], by giving her a bill of divorce. But that the Lord says this by way of permission, to avoid something worse, namely the killing of wives, just as he permitted the Jews usury towards strangers, and not absolutely or as a command, is made known from what follows: [[2:16|but iniquity shalt cover|Operiet autem iniquitas]] (the iniquity of the man who puts away his wife out of hatred, or for a cause that is not just) [[2:16|his garment|vestimentum ejus]], [[2:16|saith the Lord of hosts|dicit Dominus exercituum]], that is, he will pay the due penalty in his body in the fire of hell unless he truly repents, so that he is punished in that in which he sinned. Or: [[2:16|iniquity shalt cover his garment|Operiet iniquitas vestimentum ejus]], that is, his sin will be brought to light and shown to all at the judgment, as what lies on the surface of a garment is seen. [[2:16|keep your spirit, and despise not|Custodite spiritum vestrum, et nolite despicere]] your first and lawful wife. Hence Christ teaches in the Gospel that a wife is not to be put away[[Matt 5:32||]], [[Matt 19:9|except it be for fornication|nisi ob fornicationem]]: and not even then is she let go as to the marriage bond, since that is indissoluble after carnal union, but as to cohabitation and bed.

paras.t: Insuper redarguuntur Judæi de alio grandi peccato in Deum. Laborare fecistis Dominum in sermonibus vestris, id est, per verba vestra blasphema, incredulitatis ac diffidentiæ plena, Deum quodammodo molestastis. Loquitur autem de Deo modo humano, quasi de homine ex aliorum malis afflicto. Unde et Dominus ait in Isaia: Laboravi sustinens. Alibi quoque ait Dominus populo Judæorum: Præbuisti mihi laborem in iniquitatibus tuis. Similiter ait Apostolus: Nolite contristare Spiritum Sanctum Dei. Et dixistis: In quo eum fecimus laborare? Videlicet, In eo quod dicitis: Omnis qui facit malum, bonus est in conspectu Domini, et tales ei placent. Infirmi enim Judæi futurum Dei judicium non pensantes, sed præsentis vitæ prosperitatem ac remunerationem imprudenter considerantes, negabant quodammodo providentiam Dei, vel Deum esse peccatorum fautorem censebant: eo quod viderant gentiles in gyro eorum morantes, Persas quoque et Medos, in hoc sæculo prosperari, ditari, regnare, qui tamen Deum Israel non colebant; se vero Deum colentes, in hac vita conculcari, depauperari, atque diversis miseriis affici. Unde in eorum persona fertur in Psalmo: Et dixerunt: Quomodo scit Deus? et, Si est scientia in Excelso? Aut certe ubi est Deus judicii? id est, si aliter est, et si mali Deo displicent, bonique placent, ubi est tunc justum ejus judicium, quod exigit malos puniri ac dejici, bonos autem exaltari et glorificari? De isto jam celeriter curro, quoniam in sequenti capitulo plenius inde, Deo agente, dicetur.
paras.en: Further, the Jews are rebuked for another great sin against God. [[2:17|You have wearied the Lord with your words|Laborare fecistis Dominum in sermonibus vestris]], that is, by your blasphemous words, full of unbelief and distrust, you have in a manner troubled God. He speaks of God in a human way, as of a man afflicted by the wrongs of others. Hence the Lord says in Isaias too: [[Is 1:14|I am weary of bearing them|Laboravi sustinens]] [*Laboravi*, 'I have laboured': the word behind 'wearied' in this verse, *Laborare fecistis*, 'you have made to labour']. Elsewhere also the Lord says to the people of the Jews: [[Is 43:24|thou hast wearied me with thy iniquities|Præbuisti mihi laborem in iniquitatibus tuis]]. Likewise the Apostle says: [[Eph 4:30|grieve not the holy Spirit of God|Nolite contristare Spiritum Sanctum Dei]]. [[2:17|and you said: Wherein have we wearied him|Et dixistis: In quo eum fecimus laborare]]? Namely, [[2:17|In that you say|In eo quod dicitis]]: [[2:17|Every one that doth evil, is good in the sight of the Lord, and such please him|Omnis qui facit malum, bonus est in conspectu Domini, et tales ei placent]]. For the weak Jews, not weighing the future judgment of God but imprudently considering the prosperity and reward of the present life, in a manner denied the providence of God, or held God to be a favourer of sinners: because they had seen the gentiles dwelling round about them, and the Persians and Medes too, prospering in this world, growing rich and reigning, though they did not worship the God of Israel; while they themselves, who worshipped God, were trodden down in this life, impoverished, and afflicted with divers miseries. Hence in their person it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 72:11|And they said: How doth God know? and is there knowledge in the most High?|Et dixerunt: Quomodo scit Deus? et, Si est scientia in Excelso?]] [[2:17|or surely where is the God of judgment|Aut certe ubi est Deus judicii]]? that is, if it is otherwise, and the wicked displease God and the good please him, where then is his just judgment, which requires that the wicked be punished and cast down, and the good exalted and glorified? Over this I now pass quickly, since more will be said of it in the following chapter, God working with me.

2.title: De mystico ejusdem capituli secundi sensu.
2.title_en: Of the mystical sense of the same second chapter.

paras.t: Facile prorsus est ad sacerdotes novi Testamenti applicari, quod in præsentis capituli capite de veteris Testamenti sacerdotibus dictum est. Et nunc ad vos mandatum hoc vivendi sacerdotaliter, sobrie, caste, exemplariter ac devote, o sacerdotes evangelicæ legis : qui tanto amplius ad spiritualem virtuosamque obligamini vitam, quam sacerdotes Mosaicæ legis, quanto sacerdotium Christi spiritualius, divinius, atque sublimius est sacerdotio illo legali.
paras.en: What is said at the head of the present chapter about the priests of the Old Testament can very easily be applied to the priests of the New. [[2:1|And now|Et nunc]] [[2:1|this commandment is to you|ad vos mandatum hoc]], the commandment to live as priests, soberly, chastely, as an example to others and devoutly, [[2:1|O ye priests|o sacerdotes]] of the gospel law: who are bound to a spiritual and virtuous life so much more than the priests of the law of Moses, as the priesthood of Christ is more spiritual, more divine and more sublime than that priesthood of the law.

paras.t: Si nolueritis audire, id est præcepta vivendi sacerdotibus Christi specialiter tradita adimplere, mittam in vos egestatem, id est donorum gratiæ gratum faciendis carentiam, ut singulis vobis conveniat illud Apocalypsis : Tu es miser et miserabilis, pauper, cæcus et nudus; et maledicam benedictionibus vestris : id est, bona naturæ, bona fortunæ, et bona Ecclesiæ vobis concessa, convertam vobis in majorem damnationem, et permittam vos illis abuti in superbiam; eritque damnatio vestra tanto pœnalior, quanto plura a me bona fuistis sortiti. Unde et Christus in Evangelio profitetur : Cui plus donatum est, plus repetetur ab eo. Quoniam non posuistis super cor, id est, ineffabilem magnitudinem beneficiorum meorum non ponderastis, videlicet quanta sit dignitas sacerdotii vestri, quanta liberalitas atque dignatio Christi in Sacramento se ipsum vobis donantis, et cum quanta reverentia puritateque mentis Sacramentum hoc conficere, sumere et tractare oportet.
paras.en: [[2:2|If you will not hear|Si nolueritis audire]], that is, if you will not fulfil the precepts of living handed down especially to the priests of Christ, [[2:2|I will send poverty upon you|mittam in vos egestatem]], that is, a lack of the gifts of sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes a man pleasing to God], so that the word of the Apocalypse may fit each one of you: [[Apoc 3:17|thou art wretched and miserable and poor and blind and naked|Tu es miser et miserabilis, pauper, cæcus et nudus]]; [[2:2|and will curse your blessings|et maledicam benedictionibus vestris]]: that is, the goods of nature, the goods of fortune and the goods of the Church granted to you I will turn to your greater damnation, and I will let you abuse them to pride; and your damnation will be the more painful, the more goods you have received from me as your lot. Hence Christ too declares in the Gospel: [[Luke 12:48|unto whomsoever much is given, of him much shall be required|Cui plus donatum est, plus repetetur ab eo]]. [[2:2|Because you have not laid it to heart|Quoniam non posuistis super cor]], that is, you have not weighed the unspeakable greatness of my benefits: namely, how great is the dignity of your priesthood, how great the generosity and condescension of Christ, who gives himself to you in the Sacrament, and with what reverence and purity of mind this Sacrament must be consecrated, received and handled.

paras.t: Ecce ego projiciam vobis brachium, id est, opera vestra tanquam indigna repellam, et gratiæ vigorem suspendam; et dispergam super vultum vestrum stercus solennitatum vestrarum, id est, vitia vestra carnalia, et vitam vestram fœdam ac turpem, vobis cum grandi confusione vestra objiciam et cunctis ostendam; et assumet vos secum : opera enim vestra sequentur vos. Et scietis per experientiam confusionis damnationisque vestræ, quia misi ad vos mandatum istud novæ legis.
paras.en: [[2:3|Behold, I will cast the shoulder to you|Ecce ego projiciam vobis brachium]] [*brachium*, literally "arm"], that is, I will thrust back your works as unworthy and withhold the strength of grace; [[2:3|and will scatter upon your face the dung of your solemnities|et dispergam super vultum vestrum stercus solennitatum vestrarum]], that is, I will cast your carnal vices and your foul and shameful life in your teeth, to your great confusion, and show them to all; [[2:3|and it shall take you away with it|et assumet vos secum]]: for your works shall follow you[[Apoc 14:13||]]. [[2:4|And you shall know|Et scietis]], by the experience of your confusion and damnation, [[2:4|that I sent you this commandment|quia misi ad vos mandatum istud]] of the new law.

paras.t: Pactum meum, id est novi Testamenti fœdus, fuit cum eo, præsertim cum Apostolis eorumque successoribus sanctis : quod est pactum vitæ gratiæ in præsenti, et vitæ gloriæ in futuro, et pactum pacis internæ. Siquidem coram illis in Cœna Christus novi Testamenti Sacramentum instituit, et novum Testamentum firmavit.
paras.en: [[2:5|My covenant|Pactum meum]], that is, the covenant of the New Testament, [[2:5|was with him|fuit cum eo]], above all with the Apostles and their holy successors: which is a covenant [[2:5|of life|vitæ]], of the life of grace in the present and the life of glory in the future, and a covenant of inward [[2:5|peace|pacis]]. For it was before them, at the Supper, that Christ instituted the Sacrament of the New Testament[[Matt 26:26||]] and confirmed the new testament[[Matt 26:28||]].

paras.t: Denique de quolibet Apostolorum et sacerdotum atque pontificum, sancte viventium, dici potest secundum præcedenti articulo positum, quod Dominus ait : Dedi ei timorem, et timuit me, etc. Lex veritatis, id est doctrina et jussio Christi, fuit in ore ejus, et iniquitas non est inventa in labiis ejus; in pace et in æquitate ambulavit mecum, et multos avertit ab iniquitate. Secundum Hieronymum, his verbis describit Deus, qualis esse debeat sacerdos, scilicet ut fideliter timeat Deum, et legem divinam semper habens in corde et ore, nullo maculetur mendacio, nec impietate turpetur aut dolo, sed cum pace et justitia coram Altissimo vivens, ceteros præsertim sibi commissos, semper totis viribus ab impietate avertere satagat : quia ut ait Hieronymus, qui sacerdos est, et non corripit delinquentes, sacerdotis officium præterit.
paras.en: Further, of any of the Apostles, priests and bishops who live holily, there can be said, as was set out in the preceding article, what the Lord says: [[2:5|I gave him fear: and he feared me|Dedi ei timorem, et timuit me]], etc. [[2:6|The law of truth|Lex veritatis]], that is, the teaching and command of Christ, [[2:6|was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace, and in equity, and turned many away from iniquity|fuit in ore ejus, et iniquitas non est inventa in labiis ejus; in pace et in æquitate ambulavit mecum, et multos avertit ab iniquitate]]. According to Jerome, in these words God describes what a priest ought to be: namely, that he should faithfully fear God and, having the divine law always in his heart and mouth, be stained by no lie nor defiled by impiety or guile, but, living in peace and justice before the Most High, strive always with all his strength to turn others, especially those entrusted to him, away from impiety: for, as Jerome says, he who is a priest and does not rebuke wrongdoers neglects the office of a priest.

paras.t: Labia enim sacerdotis custodiunt scientiam. Sacerdotum est habere discretionem præcipuam inter virtutes ac vitia, inter pretiosum et vile, inter bonum et malum, inter verum et falsum, inter lepram et non lepram, et ut in tantum eruditi sint, quod onus sui officii fructuose queant implere, aliosque docere. Nam legem, id est Christi præcepta et documenta, requirent laici ex ore ejus : præsertim quum in Levitico Dominus dicat sacerdotibus veteris Testamenti : Vinum et omne quod inebriare potest, non bibetis, quando intrabitis in tabernaculum testimonii, ut habeatis scientiam discernendi inter sanctum et profanum, doceatisque filios Israel omnia legitima mea. Quam vehementer ergo damnabiles sunt sacerdotes novi Testamenti, qui potibus vacant, et sanctæ Scripturæ studium non frequentant!
paras.en: [[2:7|For the lips of the priests shall keep knowledge|Labia enim sacerdotis custodiunt scientiam]]. It belongs to priests to have an outstanding discernment between virtues and vices, between the precious and the vile, between good and evil, between true and false, between leprosy and not leprosy, and to be so learned that they can fulfil the burden of their office fruitfully and teach others. For [[2:7|the law|legem]], that is, the precepts and teachings of Christ, the laity [[2:7|shall seek|requirent]] [[2:7|at his mouth|ex ore ejus]]: all the more since in Leviticus the Lord says to the priests of the Old Testament: [[Lev 10:9|You shall not drink wine nor any thing that may make drunk|Vinum et omne quod inebriare potest, non bibetis]], [[Lev 10:9|when you enter into the tabernacle of the testimony|quando intrabitis in tabernaculum testimonii]], [[Lev 10:10|And that you may have knowledge to discern between holy and unholy|ut habeatis scientiam discernendi inter sanctum et profanum]], [[Lev 10:11|And may teach the children of Israel all my ordinances|doceatisque filios Israel omnia legitima mea]]. How exceedingly damnable, then, are the priests of the New Testament who give their time to drinking and do not apply themselves to the study of Holy Scripture!

paras.t: Vos autem recessistis de via, et scandalizastis plurimos in lege. Hoc, proh dolor! non expositione, sed luctu et gemitu indiget, quum sacerdotes Christi de via justitiæ impudenter ac publice nimis recedant, suaque perditissima conversatione innumerabiles graviter scandalizent. Ideo Dominus dat eos contemptibiles vulgo et omnibus, ita ut laici sacerdotibus vix assurgant, vel reverentiæ exiguum signum demonstrent, quin potius eos irrident.
paras.en: [[2:8|But you have departed out of the way, and have caused many to stumble at the law|Vos autem recessistis de via, et scandalizastis plurimos in lege]]. This, alas, needs no exposition, but mourning and groaning, since the priests of Christ depart from the way of justice shamelessly and all too publicly, and by their most abandoned way of life gravely scandalize countless people. Therefore the Lord makes them contemptible to the common people and to all, so that the laity scarcely rise for priests or show the least sign of reverence; rather, they mock them.

paras.t: Porro quod subditur, Numquid non pater unus omnium nostrum? numquid non Deus unus creavit nos? quare ergo despicit unusquisque nostrum fratrem suum? contra omnes superbos, indignabundos, passionatosque dicitur, qui communem originem atque naturæ parilitatem non attendentes, facili occasione despiciunt alios : in quo tam sæculares, nobiles, potentes, ac divites, quam alii quidam in propriis oculis sapientes aut virtuosi, multum culpabiles sunt, non intendentes quod nihil boni habeant, nisi a Deo, et quod vitiis pleni sunt, Deo odibiles, quum hi quos spernunt, multis forte donis gratiæ decorentur, vel decorabuntur. Ideo ad Romanos dicit Apostolus : Tu quid judicas fratrem tuum? aut tu quare spernis fratrem tuum? omnes enim stabimus ante tribunal Christi. Attendat igitur omnis Christianus, quod loquitur Christus : Qui major est vestrum, sit vester minister.
paras.en: Next, what follows, [[2:10|Have we not all one father? hath not one God created us? why then doth every one of us despise his brother|Numquid non pater unus omnium nostrum? numquid non Deus unus creavit nos? quare ergo despicit unusquisque nostrum fratrem suum?]]? is said against all the proud, the indignant and the passionate, who, not heeding their common origin and the equality of their nature, despise others on slight occasion. In this, worldly people, nobles, the powerful and the rich, as well as certain others who are wise or virtuous in their own eyes, are much to blame, not considering that they have nothing good except from God, and that they are full of vices and hateful to God, while those whom they spurn are perhaps adorned, or will be adorned, with many gifts of grace. Therefore the Apostle says to the Romans: [[Rom 14:10|thou, why judgest thou thy brother? Or thou, why dost thou despise thy brother? For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ|Tu quid judicas fratrem tuum? aut tu quare spernis fratrem tuum? omnes enim stabimus ante tribunal Christi]]. Let every Christian, then, heed what Christ says: [[Matt 23:11|He that is the greatest among you|Qui major est vestrum]], [[Matt 20:26|let him be your minister|sit vester minister]] [the margin gives Matt. xx, 26 and xxiii, 11; Denis joins the two].

paras.t: Transgressus est Juda, id est plebs christiana confitens Deo, quando secundum fidem suam condigne non vivit; et abominatio facta est in Israel, id est in contemplativis, dum hi qui spiritu incipiunt, carne consummantur, et in Jerusalem, id est in ministris Ecclesiæ, quando sacerdos vivit ut populus; quia contaminavit Judas sanctificationem Domini, id est, post opera pœnitentiæ Deo placita recidivavit, et in ecclesia loquaciter, vage et irreligiose se habuit, sicut (heu!) quotidie cernimus, et habuit filiam dei alieni, id est, iniquitatem sibi quasi in conjugem sumpsit, actus immundos jugiter amando et amplectendo. Hoc faciunt carnales et lubrici quorum deus venter est, et cupidi qui aurum Deo præponunt. Disperdat Dominus virum qui fecerit hoc, nisi desistat.
paras.en: [[2:11|Juda hath transgressed|Transgressus est Juda]], that is, the Christian people that confesses God [Juda is taken to mean "confession"], when it does not live worthily of its faith; [[2:11|and abomination hath been committed in Israel|et abominatio facta est in Israel]], that is, among the contemplatives [Israel is taken to mean "seeing God"], when those who begin in the spirit are finished in the flesh[[Gal 3:3||]], [[2:11|and in Jerusalem|et in Jerusalem]], that is, among the ministers of the Church, when the priest lives like the people; [[2:11|for Juda hath profaned the holiness of the Lord|quia contaminavit Judas sanctificationem Domini]], that is, after works of penance pleasing to God he has relapsed, and has behaved in church talkatively, restlessly and irreverently, as (alas!) we see daily, [[2:11|and hath married the daughter of a strange god|et habuit filiam dei alieni]], that is, he has taken iniquity to himself as a wife, by constantly loving and embracing unclean acts. This is done by the carnal and the lustful, [[Phil 3:19|whose God is their belly|quorum deus venter est]], and by the covetous, who put gold before God. [[2:12|The Lord will cut off the man that hath done this|Disperdat Dominus virum qui fecerit hoc]], unless he desist [Denis reads *Disperdat*, "may the Lord cut off", and adds "unless he desist"].

paras.t: Operiebatis lacrimis altare Domini, fletu et gemitu. Hoc faciunt, qui alios opprimunt et contristant, ita ut illi ita afflicti, coram Domino ingemiscant et plorent. Rursus id faciunt, qui pro temporalium amissione ac damno terreno superflue lugent ac dolent. Horum opera et oblata Deo non complacent.
paras.en: [[2:13|you have covered the altar of the Lord with tears, with weeping, and bellowing|Operiebatis lacrimis altare Domini, fletu et gemitu]] [Denis reads *gemitu*, "groaning", for the Vulgate's *mugitu*, "bellowing"]. This is done by those who oppress and grieve others, so that those so afflicted groan and weep before the Lord. Again, it is done by those who mourn and grieve beyond measure over the loss of temporal things and earthly harm. The works and offerings of these do not please God.

paras.t: Denique, quod hic dicitur contra odientes conjuges suas, intelligi potest contra Christianos qui uxores suas despiciunt, et velut famulas tractant, præsertim contra adulteros omni damnatione dignissimos. Hi igitur sunt docendi, ut pensent se et conjuges suas ab uno Deo esse creatos, et ideo copulatos ut socialiter amicabiliterque simul viventes, procreent filios, in quibus cultus Dei amplificetur.
paras.en: Lastly, what is said here against those who hate their wives can be understood against Christians who despise their wives and treat them like servant girls, and above all against adulterers, who are most worthy of every damnation. These, then, are to be taught to consider that they and their wives were created by the one God, and were joined so that, living together as companions and friends, they might beget children in whom the worship of God might be increased.

paras.t: Custodite spiritum vestrum in timore et humilitate, proprias ærumnas efficaciter intuendo, omneque bonum Deo adscribendo, et nolite despicere quemquam, præsertim propter paupertatem, vel naturalem defectum. Nihilo minus impii et mundani, secundum quod tales, in communi spernendi sunt, sicut de viro justo cantamus in Psalmo : Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus, timentes autem Dominum glorificat. Hinc sanctus Job : Si contempsi, inquit, judicium subire cum servo meo. Numquid non in utero fecit me, qui et illum?
paras.en: [[2:16|keep your spirit|Custodite spiritum vestrum]] in fear and humility, looking earnestly at your own miseries and ascribing every good to God, [[2:16|and despise not|et nolite despicere]] anyone, especially for poverty or a natural defect. Nevertheless the wicked and worldly, as such, are in general to be spurned, as we sing in the Psalm of the just man: [[Ps 14:4|In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing: but he glorifieth them that fear the Lord|Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus, timentes autem Dominum glorificat]]. Hence holy Job says: [[Job 31:13|If I have despised|Si contempsi]], he says, [[Job 31:13|to abide judgment with my manservant|judicium subire cum servo meo]]. [[Job 31:15|Did not he that made me in the womb make him also|Numquid non in utero fecit me, qui et illum]]?

paras.t: Laborare fecistis Dominum in sermonibus vestris; et dixistis : In quo eum facimus laborare? In eo quod dicitis : Omnis qui facit malum, bonus est in conspectu Domini, et tales ei placent. Aut certe ubi est Deus judicii ? Hoc juxta intellectum præhabitum intelligi potest de imperfectis et rudibus Christianis, qui visa impiorum prosperitate, justorumque tribulatione, contra Deum murmurant, atque ipsius providentiæ detrahunt, quemadmodum sequenti capitulo clarius innotescet. Cetera ex præinductis facillime intelliguntur.
paras.en: [[2:17|You have wearied the Lord with your words, and you said: Wherein have we wearied him? In that you say: Every one that doth evil, is good in the sight of the Lord, and such please him: or surely where is the God of judgment?|Laborare fecistis Dominum in sermonibus vestris; et dixistis : In quo eum facimus laborare? In eo quod dicitis : Omnis qui facit malum, bonus est in conspectu Domini, et tales ei placent. Aut certe ubi est Deus judicii]] This, following the sense given before, can be understood of imperfect and unlearned Christians who, seeing the prosperity of the wicked and the tribulation of the just, murmur against God and disparage his providence, as will be made plainer in the next chapter. The rest is very easily understood from what has been set down before.
